reason: While the text depicts Yahweh as all-powerful, it explicitly contradicts the characterization of being 'emotionally removed' and poorly supports 'remote.' The passage emphasizes God's direct, personal engagement: God 'sees' (וַיַּ֥רְא) that Moses turned aside, actively calls to him by name, identifies himself with the patriarchs, explicitly states 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to me and I have also seen the oppression' (צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י וְגַם־ רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הַלַּ֔חַץ), and promises 'I will be with you' (אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ). These verses demonstrate emotional awareness of human suffering and responsive commitment to action—the opposite of emotional removal. God initiates covenant relationship with Moses and responds directly to human need.
